purpose: One data-only source/ATR timing observation supporting M5 Entry; no model, labels, signal selection, broker account lookup or trading.
request_binding: Before any GET, claim the exact UTC interval, native owner request parameters and source SHA set. Three M5 chunks cover 35 calendar days; one M1 chunk covers the final five minutes. Never retry or resume. Any unknown request outcome consumes its attempt.
scope_limits: Fresh source bundles only, in the separate CAPTURE directory; never load the sealed native TEST dataset or existing December outcomes.
ATR uses the unchanged five-TF numerical owner and explicit 35-day probe origin. This is not original TRAIN/serve numerical parity or a complete model-input snapshot.
M1-derived context remains allowed only on M5 Entry issues. No M1 Entry, open-trade monitoring, Exit, orders or model invocation.
No UTC accuracy bound is guessed or inferred from a sync flag. Without independently qualified bounds the absolute readiness result remains UNKNOWN.
The probe can measure physical source and calculation events; it cannot restore missing original 2024 quote order or demonstrate Entry edge.
stop_rule: One claim and four maximum HTTP attempts. Missing any of the five M1 minutes, the declared ending M5 bar, ATR support, source binding or transport success ends the observation. Preserve all partial artifacts. No automatic new slot.
deadline_semantics: Total-run TERM at 900 seconds, KILL after 10 more seconds. Worker verifies actual timeout parent and matching arguments; the cap covers validation and ATR after transport too.
execution_authority: Only the exact explicit NEXT_RUN_POLICY collection admission can permit execution. This immutable plan itself grants no authority.
timing_semantics: The preclaimed M5 bar close is the historical event-time comparison boundary. Physical receipt and input publication occur at their separately recorded times. This probe issues no Entry or forecast and introduces no operational zero-latency requirement or fixed Entry delay.
